convention: Equirect as three.js samples it (equirectUv: u = atan2(d.z, d.x)/2pi + 0.5, v = asin(d.y)/pi + 0.5, image top = +Y). With three = (Blender X, Blender Z, -Blender Y) this is identical to Blender's world Environment Texture mapping (u = 0.5 - atan2(bY, bX)/2pi), so rotationY = 0 in three.js matches an unrotated Blender world. The image centre (u=0.5) faces three.js +X (= Blender +X); u=0.25 faces three.js -Z (Blender +Y).
sunAzimuthConvention: degrees from three.js -Z towards +X (clockwise seen from above)
backdropToneMap: extended Reinhard, white point 4.0, per channel, then sRGB OETF
